completion_policy.content_complete: Requires manually verified or content-verified alignment and all mandatory learning fields: objectives, prerequisites, introduction, explanations, applicable definitions, worked examples, notation where needed, practice, knowledge check and summary.
completion_policy.assessment_complete: Requires at least assessment_question_target distinct, aligned questions with validated prompts, correct answers, explanations, learning-objective coverage, non-duplicate items and appropriate difficulty variation. No external quality review is claimed by structural checks.
completion_policy.overall_complete: Requires content complete, assessment complete and manually or content-verified lesson alignment. Educator review and publication remain separate statuses.
completion_policy.review_complete: Requires an explicitly recorded qualified educator review; no such review is claimed in this baseline.
completion_policy.published: Requires an actual published state in the learner CMS; the separate static Mathematics pack is served to learners but is not represented as a CMS-published lesson.

instructional_evidence: Classify common numbers as rational or irrational.
Explain relationships among whole numbers, integers, rational numbers and real numbers.
Evaluate expressions using grouping, powers and left-to-right operation rules.

missing_instructional_content: Explicit natural-versus-whole-number classification and boundary cases.
Topic-specific worked examples, guided practice and a topic summary.

Compare integers using their positions.
Explain absolute value as distance from zero.

number-systems/natural-numbers.definition: Counting numbers used to represent a count; conventions differ on whether zero is included.
number-systems/natural-numbers.learning_scope: Use positive counting numbers for finite counts, state the convention for zero, and distinguish count from position or measurement.
expected_learning_outcomes: Classify positive counting numbers under a stated convention.
Explain how including or excluding zero changes the natural-number set.
Use a natural number to represent a count in a simple context.
prerequisite_knowledge: Recognize zero as an empty count.
concepts_to_teach: Natural numbers as counts rather than signed changes.
skills: Classify values using a declared convention.
Explain a boundary case such as zero.
Translate a count context into a natural number.
misconceptions: Every text includes zero in the natural numbers.
Zero represents a positive count.

number-systems/whole-numbers.definition: The non-negative integers: zero and the positive counting numbers.
number-systems/whole-numbers.learning_scope: Classify whole numbers, interpret zero in count contexts, and distinguish whole numbers from integers and non-integer values.
expected_learning_outcomes: Identify whole numbers in a mixed list.
Explain why zero is a whole number.
Distinguish a negative integer and a fraction from a whole number.
Represent a whole-number count in a context.
concepts_to_teach: Negative values and non-integers are outside the set.
Whole numbers are a subset of integers.
skills: Classify a value by set membership.
Use set inclusion to explain classification.
Interpret zero as none in a count context.
misconceptions: Zero is not a number.
All integers are whole numbers.
A positive fraction is a whole number.

number-systems/integers.definition: The set containing zero, positive whole numbers, and their negative opposites.
number-systems/integers.learning_scope: Classify integers and use them in signed arithmetic, including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by non-zero integers.
expected_learning_outcomes: Identify integers and non-integers in a set.
Add and subtract signed integers using direction or additive inverses.
Multiply and divide non-zero integers using sign and magnitude.
Explain why division by zero is undefined.
prerequisite_knowledge: Whole-number addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.
concepts_to_teach: Signed operation rules and division by zero.
misconceptions: A negative integer is not an integer.
Subtracting always makes a number smaller.
A negative times a negative is negative.
Division by zero equals zero.

number-systems/positive-and-negative-num.definition: Signed numbers that indicate direction or position relative to a chosen reference value.
number-systems/positive-and-negative-num.learning_scope: Interpret signs in contexts, identify opposites and absolute value as distance, and calculate signed changes.
expected_learning_outcomes: Assign positive or negative values relative to a stated reference.
Find the opposite and absolute value of an integer.
Explain why subtracting a negative changes direction.
Calculate a sequence of signed changes and interpret the result.
misconceptions: A negative value is always less useful or smaller in magnitude.
Absolute value retains the negative sign.
Subtracting a negative moves left.

number-systems/number-lines.definition: A scale with equally spaced positions representing ordered numbers around a reference point.
number-systems/number-lines.learning_scope: Read, label and use a number line to represent signed integers, opposites, distance, and arithmetic movement.
expected_learning_outcomes: Place zero and signed integers on an equally spaced line.
Show an addition or subtraction as directed movement.
Use equal spacing to locate opposites.
Infer and explain an unknown point from labeled intervals.
Distinguish a signed position from non-negative distance traveled.
misconceptions: Tick marks can have unequal values without a changed scale.
Moving left is always a negative final coordinate.
Distance is signed.

number-systems/comparing-and-ordering-nu.definition: Determining relative size and arranging values from least to greatest or greatest to least.
number-systems/comparing-and-ordering-nu.learning_scope: Compare integers by number-line position and order signed values without confusing magnitude with value.
expected_learning_outcomes: Use <, >, and = correctly for signed integers.
Order a mixed list of negative, zero and positive integers.
Explain comparisons using position or distance from zero.
Identify and correct an ordering error.
concepts_to_teach: Negative values reverse the magnitude intuition.
Zero separates negative and positive values.
misconceptions: -9 is greater than -2 because 9 > 2.
Zero is positive or negative.
The inequality symbol points toward the larger value.

number-systems/factors.definition: A positive whole number that divides another whole number exactly.
number-systems/factors.learning_scope: Find and verify factor pairs, distinguish factors from multiples, and apply common factors to equal grouping.
expected_learning_outcomes: List all positive factors of a whole number.
Verify a factor using exact division.
Use factor pairs to identify a missing factor.
Select a common factor to describe equal grouping.
misconceptions: A number's multiples are its factors.
A factor larger than the number is possible among positive factors.
A remainder can be ignored.

number-systems/multiples.definition: Products of a number and an integer multiplier; positive multiples arise from positive whole-number multipliers.
number-systems/multiples.learning_scope: Generate multiples, test divisibility, and find common and least common multiples in repeated-event contexts.
expected_learning_outcomes: Generate positive multiples in sequence.
Determine whether a value is a multiple by division or multiplication.
Find a common multiple of two values.
Explain why a selected common multiple is or is not the least.
prerequisite_knowledge: Recognize equal intervals and repeated cycles.
misconceptions: A multiple is always smaller than its factor.
Any common multiple is the LCM.
Zero is the least positive multiple.

number-systems/prime-numbers.definition: A whole number greater than one with exactly two positive factors: one and itself.
number-systems/prime-numbers.learning_scope: Classify primes, explain the boundary cases zero and one, and use divisibility tests to check candidate factors.
expected_learning_outcomes: Classify a whole number greater than one as prime or composite.
Explain why one is not prime.
Check prime candidates using divisors up to the square root.
Use primes as factors in a prime factorisation.
prerequisite_knowledge: Square numbers and approximate square roots.
concepts_to_teach: One is neither prime nor composite.
Prime testing and prime building blocks.
misconceptions: One is prime.
Every odd number is prime.
A number is prime if no small divisor was tried.

number-systems/composite-numbers.definition: A whole number greater than one with more than two positive factors.
number-systems/composite-numbers.learning_scope: Identify a non-trivial factor pair as evidence of compositeness and distinguish composite values from one and primes.
expected_learning_outcomes: Classify composite values using a non-trivial factor pair.
Explain why one is not composite.
Find a divisor that disproves a prime claim.
Relate composite values to products of primes.
misconceptions: One is composite.
All even numbers are composite including 2.
Odd means prime.

number-systems/prime-factorization.definition: A representation of a composite positive integer as a product of prime factors.
number-systems/prime-factorization.learning_scope: Construct, check and use prime factorisations, including index notation for repeated primes.
expected_learning_outcomes: Build a factor tree until all leaves are prime.
Write repeated prime factors using powers.
Verify a factorisation by multiplication.
Use prime powers to compare factor structures.
misconceptions: Stop at a composite leaf.
Different tree shapes imply different prime factorisations.
Forget multiplicity when listing primes.

number-systems/divisibility-rules.definition: Tests that determine exact divisibility by using digit structure or place value.
number-systems/divisibility-rules.learning_scope: Apply and justify divisibility rules for 2, 3, 5, 9 and 10; use tests to identify factors and simplify calculations.
expected_learning_outcomes: Apply the last-digit tests for 2, 5 and 10.
Apply digit-sum tests for 3 and 9.
Determine divisibility by more than one divisor.
Explain a divisibility result using the relevant rule.
misconceptions: Digit-sum rule checks only the last digit.
Divisibility by 3 implies divisibility by 9.
A test gives the quotient.

number-systems/highest-common-factor-hcf.definition: The greatest positive integer that divides each number in a specified set exactly.
number-systems/highest-common-factor-hcf.learning_scope: Find HCFs by factor lists or prime powers, verify the result, and apply it to largest equal groups or pieces.
expected_learning_outcomes: Find common factors and select the greatest.
Find HCF using prime factorisations.
Verify that the HCF divides every input.
Model a largest-equal-group context using HCF.
prerequisite_knowledge: Interpret equal groups and no remainders.
misconceptions: HCF is the largest input.
Use maximum prime powers for HCF.
Confuse HCF with LCM.

number-systems/lowest-common-multiple-lc.definition: The least positive integer that is a multiple of each number in a specified set.
number-systems/lowest-common-multiple-lc.learning_scope: Find LCMs by listing multiples or prime powers, verify the result, and apply it to repeating intervals.
expected_learning_outcomes: Identify a shared positive multiple.
Find the least common multiple using prime powers.
Verify the LCM is divisible by each input.
Model the first coincidence of repeating events.
skills: Distinguish least from any shared multiple.
Choose LCM in a cycle context.
misconceptions: Any common multiple is the LCM.
LCM uses only shared primes.
HCF and LCM use the same prime powers.

number-systems/order-of-operations.definition: A convention for evaluating grouped numerical expressions consistently.
number-systems/order-of-operations.learning_scope: Evaluate expressions with grouping, powers, roots and the four operations, respecting shared precedence and left-to-right order.
expected_learning_outcomes: Evaluate nested brackets from the inside outward.
Apply powers and roots before multiplication or division.
Evaluate multiplication/division left to right.
Evaluate addition/subtraction left to right and check by estimation.
concepts_to_teach: Shared precedence for multiplication/division and addition/subtraction.
misconceptions: BODMAS means multiplication always precedes division.
Addition always precedes subtraction.
An estimate is the exact answer.

number-systems/exponents-and-powers.definition: A power represents repeated multiplication of equal bases, with index laws extending the notation for non-zero bases.
number-systems/exponents-and-powers.learning_scope: Interpret bases and indices; evaluate powers; apply product, quotient, zero and negative-index laws; express positive quantities in standard form.
expected_learning_outcomes: Identify the base and index in a power.
Evaluate integer powers and apply equal-base index laws.
Explain zero and negative indices for non-zero bases.
Convert large and small positive quantities to standard form.
prerequisite_knowledge: Place value and powers of ten.
skills: Normalize standard form and check exponent sign.
misconceptions: aⁿ means a×n.
Index laws apply across different bases.
a⁰=0.
Negative index means a negative value.

number-systems/roots.definition: A root is an inverse-power value; the principal square root is non-negative while odd roots preserve sign.
number-systems/roots.learning_scope: Evaluate square and cube roots, distinguish principal roots from equation solutions, and estimate non-perfect roots by neighboring powers.
expected_learning_outcomes: Evaluate exact square and cube roots.
Distinguish √a from solutions of x²=a.
Bracket a non-perfect root between consecutive integer powers.
Refine and verify a decimal root estimate.
misconceptions: √25 equals ±5.
A negative number has a real square root.
All roots are integers.
Approximation uses an equals sign.

number-systems/squares-and-square-roots.definition: A square is n²; a perfect square has an integer square root, and √x denotes the non-negative principal root for x≥0.
number-systems/squares-and-square-roots.learning_scope: Relate square arrays and areas to squares, recognize perfect squares, evaluate principal roots and solve simple square equations.
expected_learning_outcomes: Generate and recognize perfect squares.
Evaluate principal square roots.
Explain the two solutions of x²=a for positive perfect squares.
Use area to determine a square's side length.
prerequisite_knowledge: Area of a square as side×side.
misconceptions: The square root symbol returns both signs.
A square number must look like an even number.
Side length and area have the same unit.

number-systems/cubes-and-cube-roots.definition: A cube is n³; a perfect cube has an integer cube root, which may be negative for a negative input.
number-systems/cubes-and-cube-roots.learning_scope: Evaluate cubes and cube roots, recognize perfect cubes and model cubic volume with equal unit cubes.
expected_learning_outcomes: Calculate integer cubes including negative bases.
Recognize perfect cubes and evaluate their roots.
Explain why the cube root of a negative number is negative.
Find a cube's edge from its volume.
prerequisite_knowledge: Volume of a cube as side³.
misconceptions: (-a)³ is positive.
Cube root discards the sign.
Square and cube roots behave identically for negative inputs.

number-systems/applications-of-number-sy.definition: Using number sets and operations to represent and solve quantitative situations.
number-systems/applications-of-number-sy.learning_scope: Model temperature, financial change, elevation, repeated schedules, equal grouping and multi-step calculations with suitable number concepts.
expected_learning_outcomes: Choose signed values relative to a reference in context.
Solve and interpret a multi-step signed change.
Select HCF or LCM for a grouping or repeating-event problem.
Estimate and check a contextual numerical answer with units.
misconceptions: The sign of a change is the final sign.
Use LCM for equal grouping.
Ignore units or order of operations.

data_corrections.reason: Five existing crosswalk entries used unmatched labels. The stable-ID audit maps Natural numbers and Whole numbers to existing lesson tags, Arithmetic sequences to the existing sequences-and-patterns tag, Population and sample to data-and-samples, and Translation to the existing transformations tag. These are candidate links only, not verified coverage. No lessons or question associations were added.
